mainTopic: Mixed-up bird offerings in קנים and רבי יהושע's rule, then a new משנה on invalid מליקה and the טומאה of a bird in the throat
overview: The amud opens at the end of a משנה from מסכת קנים, which the גמרא is quoting. A woman owes a required pair of birds (one חטאת and one עולה) and has also vowed bird עולות, and the כהן no longer knows how he offered them. The משנה rules that she brings five more birds, or six if two species were involved. If she also doesn't know what she gave, she brings seven, while בן עזאי requires two חטאות. רבי יהושע closes with the parable of the sheep: one sound in life, seven in death. Because רבי יהושע signs off on these rulings, they seem to clash with רב אדא בר אהבה's reading of him, that a bird עולה offered as a חטאת becomes a חטאת. The גמרא answers that רבי יהושע only meant the bird is taken out of מעילה, not that it counts toward the owner's obligation. Then a new משנה begins. It teaches that an invalid מליקה or a wrong kind of שחיטה still keeps the bird from making the eater טמא in the throat. The משנה then starts a second list of cases, whose ruling comes on the next amud.

steps.title: She must bring five more birds, all offered above the line
steps.stepSummary: The ruling for the mixed-up case: the woman brings five more birds, all offered as עולות above the red line.
steps.simpleTranslation: She must bring five more birds and have them offered above the red line.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives its ruling for the mix-up described just before this: the woman must bring five more birds. All of them are offered above the red line, the way an עולה is offered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עולה of a bird is offered above the red line on the מזבח, and a חטאת below it. Every one of these five birds goes above, so they are all עולות. They are there to make sure her vow and her required עולה are fully covered, whatever the כהן actually did.

keyTerms.meaning: Above the red line on the מזבח, where an עולה is offered
Burnt offering, burned completely on the מזבח

steps.confusionAlert: Five is not two pairs plus one by accident. The text counts single birds (פרידין), not pairs, because each bird covers a different possibility.

phrases.english: She must bring another
five birds, offered above.
phrases.notes: "Above" means above the red line on the מזבח, which is where an עולה goes.

steps.triggerLanguage: צריכה שתביא עוד חמש פרידין למעלה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the ruling for the case set up just before this text begins. This is part of a משנה from קנים that the גמרא is quoting in order to challenge רב אדא בר אהבה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the mixed-up case, the woman brings five more single birds, all offered above the red line as עולות.

steps.title: Five birds only when both pairs were one species; with two species she brings six
steps.stepSummary: The ruling of five holds only when all the birds were of one species. If two species were used, she must bring six.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is when the birds were of one species. If they were of two species, she brings six.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה narrows the ruling it just gave. Five birds is enough only when all the birds were the same kind. If two kinds were involved, she needs six.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bird offerings come from two species, תורים and בני יונה, and the pairs must match properly. When the pairs were from different species, there are more ways the כהן could have gone wrong. So one more bird is needed to cover every option.

keyTerms.meaning: Turtledoves and young pigeons, the two species used for bird offerings

phrases.english: This is when they are of one species.
But if of two species, she brings six.

steps.triggerLanguage: ממין אחד ומשני מינין תביא שש
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits step 1 to a case of one species and gives a different count for two species.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Five birds applies to one species. With two species, she brings six.

steps.title: Neither the woman nor the כהן knows what was given or done: seven birds
steps.stepSummary: A harder case: the woman doesn't know what she gave, and the כהן doesn't know what he did. She brings four birds for her vow, two for her required עולה, and one חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she gave the birds to the כהן and doesn't know what she gave, and the כהן offered them and doesn't know what he did, she needs four birds for her vow, two for her obligation, and one חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to a new case where nobody remembers anything. She doesn't know what she handed over, and the כהן doesn't know what he offered. She has to bring seven birds to cover every possibility.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Four birds, two of each species, make sure her vow is kept whichever species she promised. Two more birds, one of each species, cover her required עולה, since it may need to match whatever species the כהן used. One חטאת covers the chance that he offered everything as עולות.

keyTerms.meaning: Vow, an offering she took on by her own choice
Obligation, the required offering after giving birth
Sin offering, a bird offered below the red line

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the method of this whole section: when you can't know what happened, you bring enough offerings to cover every possibility.

phrases.english: If she gave them to the priest,
and she does not know what she gave;
and the priest went and offered them,
and he does not know what he did —
she needs four birds for her vow,
and two for her obligation,
and one sin offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: נתנתן לכהן ואינה יודעת מה נתנה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds a harder case on top of the earlier ones: now the woman is unsure too.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When neither side knows what was given or done, she brings seven birds: four for the vow, two for the obligation, and one חטאת.
steps.whatToRemember: No one knows anything, so she brings 4 + 2 + 1 = 7 birds. Every possible mistake is covered.

steps.title: בן עזאי requires two sin offerings
steps.stepSummary: בן עזאי disagrees with the single חטאת in the last case. He requires two חטאות.
steps.simpleTranslation: בן עזאי says: two sin offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: בן עזאי argues with the last ruling. Instead of one חטאת, she must bring two.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion held that one חטאת of either species is enough. בן עזאי holds that the חטאת may need to match the species the כהן used for the required עולה. So she brings one חטאת of each species, making eight birds in total.
steps.whatToRemember: The first opinion says one חטאת. בן עזאי says two, one of each species, because the חטאת may have to match the species of the עולה.

phrases.english: Ben Azzai says:
Two sin offerings.
phrases.notes: He means instead of the one חטאת in the last ruling; the rest stays the same.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the single חטאת required in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to בן עזאי, she must bring two חטאות, one of each species.

steps.title: רבי יהושע's parable of the sheep
steps.stepSummary: The quoted משנה from קנים ends with רבי יהושע's saying: a sheep makes one sound when alive and seven when dead.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע said: This is what people say: when it is alive, it has one sound, and when it is dead, it has seven sounds.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the משנה from קנים about the woman whose birds got mixed up. It ends with רבי יהושע's short parable, and that ending is what turns the quote into a challenge against רב אדא בר אהבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At first the woman owed just a simple pair of birds. Because of the mix-up and the doubts, she now has to bring seven more, like the sheep whose single voice becomes seven once it dies. Since רבי יהושע signs off on these rulings, they must follow his view. Yet they treat the mixed-up birds as not counting, which clashes with רב אדא בר אהבה's reading of him. The next step answers this.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua said: This is what people say:
When it is alive, its sound is one,
phrases.notes: He's talking about a sheep. Alive it just bleats, but after it dies its parts become seven musical instruments.

phrases.english: and when it is dead, its sound is seven.
phrases.notes: This matches step 3: four, plus two, plus one makes seven birds.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the quoted משנה from קנים that steps 1-4 were part of. רבי יהושע's endorsement makes the whole quote a challenge to רב אדא בר אהבה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The extra birds pile up because of the doubt: a simple obligation turns into seven birds.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אדא בר אהבה's explanation of רבי יהושע, that a bird עולה offered as a חטאת becomes a valid חטאת. The קנים rulings, which רבי יהושע endorses, still require replacement birds.

steps.title: רבי יהושע only meant no מעילה, not that her obligation is fulfilled
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע's rule, as רב אדא בר אהבה explains it, only takes the bird out of מעילה. It does not make the bird count for the owner's obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say that רבי יהושע said this only to take it out of the law of מעילה. Did he ever say it goes up to count for her obligation?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question on רב אדא בר אהבה. רבי יהושע's rule only changes the bird's status for מעילה, so it fits with the קנים rulings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge was this: if an עולה brought as a חטאת becomes a חטאת, why must the woman in קנים bring more birds? The answer splits the rule into two parts. The bird is no longer under מעילה, but it still does not pay off her obligation. So she must bring replacements.

keyTerms.meaning: Say; you can explain it this way
Toward the obligation, so the owner's duty is fulfilled

steps.confusionAlert: Being taken out of מעילה is not the same as fulfilling the obligation. A bird can lose its הקדש status without the woman being done with her duty.
steps.whyThisMatters: This saves רב אדא בר אהבה's explanation by showing that one change in status does not bring every other result with it.

phrases.english: Say that what Rabbi Yehoshua said
was to take it out of the realm of misuse of consecrated property;
did he say it goes up to count for her obligation?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the tension created by the קנים משנה, which רבי יהושע ends, against רב אדא בר אהבה's reading of him.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If the bird becomes a חטאת, it should count fully, and the woman shouldn't need more birds.
steps.terutzMaskana: The change only takes it out of מעילה. It does not fulfill her obligation, so the קנים rulings stand.

steps.title: New משנה: invalid מליקה still does not make the bird טמא in the throat
steps.stepSummary: If someone פסול does מליקה, or it is done with the left hand or at night, or there is שחיטה of the wrong kind of bird in the wrong place, the bird is not valid. Still, it does not make the eater טמא when swallowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: All the disqualified people who pinched: their pinching is invalid, but the birds do not make a person impure in the throat. If he pinched with the left hand or at night, or slaughtered a non-sacred bird inside or a sacred bird outside, they do not make a person impure in the throat.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists cases where the מליקה or שחיטה was wrong for a קרבן, but the bird still does not carry the טומאה of a נבלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually a kosher bird that dies without a proper killing is a נבלה. It makes the person who swallows it טמא. In each of these cases the act was done wrongly, so the bird may not be eaten. Still, it counts as a proper killing as far as נבלה goes, so that טומאה does not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: People unfit to do the עבודה
They pinched the bird's neck with a thumbnail
The throat, at the moment of swallowing

steps.confusionAlert: 'Does not make טמא' does not mean you may eat it. The bird is still forbidden. It just isn't a נבלה.

phrases.english: MISHNA: All the disqualified people who pinched
their pinching is invalid,
but they do not make one impure in the throat.
phrases.notes: A kosher bird that wasn't properly killed makes the one swallowing it טמא. This bird does not.

phrases.english: If he pinched with the left hand or at night,
or slaughtered a non-sacred bird inside
or a sacred bird outside,
they do not make one impure in the throat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An invalid מליקה, and the listed kinds of שחיטה, still count as a killing, so the bird is not a נבלה that makes the eater טמא.

steps.title: The משנה begins a second list of cases
steps.stepSummary: The משנה starts listing new cases: מליקה with a knife, and מליקה of חולין inside or קדשים outside. The ruling comes in the next part of the text.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he pinched with a knife; if he pinched a non-sacred bird inside or a sacred bird outside;
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is setting up a second list of cases. Their ruling has not been said yet and comes right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These cases are not like the earlier ones. A knife is not the right tool for מליקה. And מליקה only works for a קרבן inside the עזרה, not for חולין or for something outside. So expect a different ruling from the first list.

phrases.english: If he pinched with a knife;
phrases.notes: מליקה is supposed to be done with the thumbnail, not a knife.

phrases.english: if he pinched a non-sacred bird inside
or a sacred bird outside;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets up a contrast with the cases in step 7. The ruling comes in the next part of the text.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Lists the cases of a second group. Their ruling is still to come.
